comment: Catalog of findings already verified against the Torque server source (cs2018) on a 454-blueprint calibration corpus, then checked out-of-sample against a further 73 files, so the human can skip them. 'blueprint-defect' means the blueprint really is wrong and Torque silently ignores the key - report it to the blueprint owners, there is nothing to fix in the extension. 'tool-limitation' means a known false positive of our own validator. Each 'match' is tested as a substring first and then as a regex against the finding's signature/template/message/path/section. ANYTHING NOT MATCHED HERE IS REPORTED AS **NEW** AND DESERVES INVESTIGATION: a NEW cluster is either an undocumented blueprint defect or - more interestingly - a bug in this extension's schema or validator. Add a row here only after checking the key against the Torque server source, never just to quieten the report.

'env-vars' is a grain *spec* key; placed directly on the grain it is ignored.
ActivityYaml accepts only 'commands'; env-vars under an activity is dropped, so those variables never reach the commands - move them to grain spec.env-vars.

'env-vars' is a grain *spec* key; under the grain itself or under an activity it is ignored.

An input 'style' value outside the allowed enum (e.g. 'single-select', which does not exist - the multi/single distinction is 'multi-select' vs no style at all).
A blueprint output 'kind' value outside the allowed enum (e.g. 'string'); only 'regular' and 'link' exist.
The launch form ignores per-input 'allowed-values'; declare allowed-values on the blueprint input itself.
The launch-form UI ignores section 'collapsed'; the real key is 'default_open'.
A launch-form section input must be an object with a 'name' key, not a bare string; the UI reads inputConfig.name.
'exclude' belongs under customization.layout (layout.exclude.grains / .resource-types), not directly under customization.
'.grains.<g>.status' is not a member of the grains liquid context - the members are outputs, scripts, activities and is_active.
'.envName' does not exist in the liquid context; the member is 'environmentName'.

There is no top-level .outputs context. In a workflow use '.bindings.outputs["Name"]' (PostCreationContext.Bindings -> EnvironmentBoundedContext.Outputs); in a blueprint reference the producing grain via '.grains.<grain>.outputs.<name>'.

clusters.match: Trailing period symbol is not allowed
clusters.note: A literal '{{ ... }}' written inside a shell comment or prose is still Liquid-processed by Torque and renders empty; reword or escape it.

clusters.match: The defined input 'X' is not accessed
clusters.note: Declared input is never referenced anywhere in the blueprint - dead input. Warning only.
'outputs["X"]' as a bare expression prefix is spec-1 syntax; there is no top-level outputs context in spec 2.

clusters.match: Output 'X' is not part of the outputs of command 'X' of the 'X' grain
clusters.note: An activities output is referenced but not declared in that command's 'outputs' list, so the expression resolves to nothing.

clusters.match: Output 'X' is not part of the 'X' grain's outputs
clusters.note: A grain output is referenced but not declared in that grain's spec.outputs, so the expression resolves to nothing.
False positive: a literal value that merely starts with '$' (e.g. default: $LATEST) trips the legacy spec-1 '$'-variable check.
False positive: an expression with a pipe inside a quoted filter argument (e.g. | default: "a|b") is mis-split on the '|'.
